topic: History and Types of Banks in India
description: A comprehensive study of the evolution of the Indian banking system, major phases of bank nationalization, and the classification of various banking institutions including commercial, regional, and new-age banks.

sections.title: Early History of Banking
sections.description: The inception of the banking system in India during the British era and the establishment of the early pivotal banks.

key_concepts.explanation: The 'Bank of Hindustan' was the first bank established in India in 1770 by Alexander and Company in Calcutta.

key_concepts.concept: Imperial Bank of India to SBI
key_concepts.explanation: In 1921, the three Presidency Banks (Bank of Bengal, Bank of Bombay, and Bank of Madras) were merged to form the 'Imperial Bank of India'. On the recommendation of the A.D. Gorwala Committee, it was nationalized in 1955 and renamed as the 'State Bank of India' (SBI).

sections.title: Reserve Bank of India (RBI)
sections.description: The establishment, evolution, and nationalization of India's Central Bank.

key_concepts.explanation: The RBI was established on April 1, 1935, in accordance with the provisions of the RBI Act, 1934, based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance).
Initially set up as a privately owned bank with a share capital of ₹5 Crore, the RBI was nationalized on January 1, 1949, bringing it entirely under the ownership of the Government of India.

sections.title: Nationalization of Commercial Banks
sections.description: The strategic acquisition of major private commercial banks by the Government of India to expand banking facilities to rural and priority sectors.

results: First Phase (July 19, 1969): 14 major commercial banks with deposits exceeding ₹50 Crores were nationalized.
Second Phase (April 15, 1980): 6 additional commercial banks with deposits exceeding ₹200 Crores were nationalized, bringing the total number of nationalized banks to 20 at that time.

sections.title: Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs)
sections.description: Banks that are included in the Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934, and fulfill the criterion of having a minimum paid-up capital of ₹5 Lakhs.

results: Public Sector Banks (PSBs): Banks where the Government of India holds a majority stake (51% or more) (e.g., SBI, PNB, Bank of Baroda).
Private Sector Banks: Banks where the management and control are held by private individuals or corporations (e.g., HDFC, ICICI, Axis Bank).
Foreign Banks: Banks headquartered in a foreign country but operating in India through their branches (e.g., Standard Chartered, CitiBank).

sections.title: Specialized and New Age Banks
sections.description: Niche banking institutions established for specific developmental purposes, boosting financial inclusion, and serving the unorganized sector.

key_concepts.explanation: Established on October 2, 1975, on the recommendation of the Narasimham Committee to provide credit in rural areas. The ownership ratio is strictly divided among the Central Government (50%), State Government (15%), and a Sponsor Bank (35%). 'Prathama Bank' was India's first RRB.

Set up based on the Nachiket Mor Committee recommendations to deepen financial inclusion. They can accept restricted deposits (maximum ₹2 Lakhs per customer) and offer remittance services but are strictly prohibited from issuing loans or credit cards (e.g., Airtel Payments Bank, India Post Payments Bank).

Niche banks established to provide basic banking activities to unserved and underserved sections. Unlike Payments Banks, SFBs can accept deposits of any amount and are authorized to lend money to small farmers, micro-industries, and the unorganized sector (e.g., AU Small Finance Bank, Equitas SFB).
